evidence: src/infrastructure/middleware/errorHandler.ts: function statusFor(error: unknown): number turns ValidationError/InvalidRequestError/SyntaxError into 400, NotFoundError into 404, ConflictError into 409 and anything else into 500. This is the only place that mapping exists.
src/infrastructure/middleware/errorHandler.ts: export function errorHandler(error, _req, res, _next) writes res.status(status).json({ error: message }) and hides the message on a 500.

src/infrastructure/middleware/notFoundHandler.ts: export function notFoundHandler(req, res) writes res.status(404).json({ error: `Route ${req.method} ${req.path} not found` }). It is a terminal handler for unmatched routes, part of the same error-response concern.
Minor: both files build the { error: string } JSON body directly, with no shared helper. The repetition is trivial and is not treated as a duplicated rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files in src/infrastructure/middleware serve one concern: Express middleware that ends a request with an HTTP error response. In errorHandler.ts, statusFor turns known error types into status codes (400, 404, 409, 500) and errorHandler writes the response. notFoundHandler.ts handles routes that match nothing and returns 404. Both sit at the same level, as terminal Express handlers registered by createApp.ts. The status mapping lives in one place (statusFor). The module has no shared helper that either file skips. One small issue: both files build the error body the same way, res.status(...).json({ error: ... }). That repeated format could move into one shared helper. It is two lines, though, and the 404 for an unknown route is a separate case from domain NotFoundError, so this is not a meaningful duplicated rule. It does not reach the Fail threshold.
